chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, raising it, said:

A man complained to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that his way had been cut off (by bandits), so he (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Why did you not wear a ring with the carnelian, for it is a protection from every evil.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of wearing a carnelian ring according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) prescribes wearing a carnelian ring as a means of divine protection (*hirs*) against the specific tribulation of banditry (*qat' al-tariq*). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *al-'Aqiq* not merely as a gemstone, but as a vessel for spiritual safeguarding and physical security, linking material adornment with metaphysical defense against evil forces.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, raising it, said,

‘A man complained to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> that his way had been cut-off (by the bandits), so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Why did you not wear a ring with the carnelian, for it is a protection from every evil’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ahmad in a marfu‘ manner has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a man complained before the Messenger of Allah, O Allah grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to your cause, that on the road he was robbed.
The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Why did you not wear the ring of ‘Aqiq (carnelian) which is protects from every evil matters?’”
